coordinate_convention: Planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude in -180..180, IAU2000 Mars reference (same convention as MOLA MEGDR). Positions are rover/lander touchdown points or the published centre of a selected landing ellipse.
footprint_definition: Square footprint of half-width 0.5 degrees (about 59 km N-S, 59*cos(lat) km E-W) centred on the site coordinates. Chosen to hold 17x17 MOLA MEGDR 16 ppd cells (floor/ceil edges) so slope and roughness statistics are populated; it is a REGIONAL footprint, far larger than any landing ellipse.

sites.name: Jezero Crater
sites.description: A ~45 km impact crater holding an ancient lake basin with a well-preserved river delta on its western margin. Chosen for Perseverance for its lacustrine and deltaic deposits.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Ancient lake and delta deposits (literature); no present-day ice detected at this latitude.

sites.name: Gale Crater (Bradbury Landing)
sites.heritage: NASA Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity landing site (2012)
sites.description: A 154 km crater with a 5 km central mound (Aeolis Mons / Mount Sharp) of layered sediments. Curiosity found evidence of an ancient habitable lake at Yellowknife Bay.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Fluvio-lacustrine mudstones with clay minerals (literature); no present-day ice.

sites.name: Elysium Planitia (InSight)
sites.description: Smooth, flat volcanic plains south of Elysium Mons, selected for InSight specifically because of its low relief and benign terrain.

sites.name: Oxia Planum
sites.region: Chryse Planitia margin / Mawrth Vallis region
sites.heritage: ESA ExoMars Rosalind Franklin rover selected landing site
sites.description: A clay-rich plain at the outlet of Coogoon Vallis near the dichotomy boundary, selected by ESA for its extensive Fe/Mg phyllosilicate deposits recording an ancient aqueous environment.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Extensive hydrated clay minerals from past aqueous activity (literature).

sites.name: Utopia Planitia (Viking 2)
sites.description: Northern lowland plains within the largest recognised impact basin on Mars. SHARAD radar has detected a large subsurface water-ice deposit in the region.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Subsurface water ice detected by SHARAD across Utopia Planitia (literature).

sites.name: Chryse Planitia (Viking 1)
sites.description: Low-lying plains at the mouth of the great outflow channels (Maja, Kasei, Ares Valles) that drained into the Chryse basin; the first successful Mars landing site.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Outflow-channel deposits from ancient catastrophic floods (literature); no present-day ice at the surface.

sites.name: Meridiani Planum (Opportunity)
sites.description: Flat, dark plains where TES detected coarse crystalline hematite from orbit; Opportunity confirmed sulfate-rich sandstones deposited in acidic groundwater.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Sulfate sandstones and hematite concretions from past groundwater (literature).

sites.name: Gusev Crater (Spirit)
sites.description: A 166 km crater at the outlet of Ma'adim Vallis. Expected lake sediments turned out to be olivine-bearing basaltic plains; the Columbia Hills hold altered rocks and opaline silica.
sites.water_ice_evidence: Hydrothermal silica and sulfates in the Columbia Hills (literature); plains are volcanic.
